# OPREP: Performance Optimizations in Arma 3 Update 2.20

In the world of gaming, performance is paramount, and the latest update to Arma 3, version 2.20, has made significant strides in this area. This update reflects the ongoing commitment from both the game's community and Bohemia Interactive, ensuring that players continue to enjoy a seamless experience even after 12 years since the game’s initial release.

## A Community-Driven Approach to Development

The team behind Arma 3 may be small, but it operates within a robust support network that has proven invaluable for ongoing updates and improvements. As the development team gears up for the transition to Arma 4, they remain dedicated to optimizing Arma 3, a testament to their commitment to the existing player base. Central to this process has been active community feedback, which has played a crucial role in identifying the challenges and opportunities for performance enhancements.

## Key Performance Enhancements

Update 2.20 does not introduce new multithreading capabilities; instead, it overhauls the existing multithreading code to address lag spikes and increase the minimum frames per second (FPS) experienced by players. While the maximum FPS may not see significant gains, the focus on stability and consistency is evident, as shown in performance graphs recorded with CapFrameX, which illustrate more reliable frame times.

### Command-Line Parameters Simplified

One of the main issues players faced stemmed from outdated command-line settings, often resulting in negative impacts on performance. The update provides clearer guidelines:

- **Use `-cpuCount`** to limit CPU cores effectively.
- **Avoid `-enableHT`** if using `-cpuCount`, as it becomes redundant.
- **Never use `-exThreads`.**

These updates to command-line parameters are crucial for players to optimize their gaming experience, especially with the transition towards a more multithreaded architecture.

## Shifting to 64-Bit

As part of the update, it was announced that 2.20 will be the last version to support 32-bit applications. Moving forward, the focus will shift entirely to 64-bit architecture, necessitating a shift in system requirements for optimal gameplay. The minimum and recommended specifications have been updated to ensure that new players can enjoy a realistic entry-level experience.

## The Evolution of Multithreading

The old job system, which had been in place since Arma 2, operated on a primitive model that only allowed one block of tasks to run at a time. The new Enfusion job system, however, utilizes a graph-based approach, enabling better task distribution across CPU cores. This enhancement is particularly notable in areas such as AI calculations and explosion checks, although challenges remain in ensuring that multiple threads can access the same data without issues.

title: Minimal auto-differentiation engine in Rust
description: `nanograd` is an innovative automatic-differentiation engine designed for Rust, making it easier to create and train machine learning models. This minimalistic tool, available on GitHub, has garnered attention for its performance and safety features, enabling users to efficiently compute gradients through a directed acyclic graph structure. With straightforward usage and community discussions highlighting its potential and challenges, `nanograd` is poised to enhance the Rust ecosystem in the field of machine learning.
